_README: Declared, intentional differences between the Postgres schema (migrations/) and
Every entry needs a REASON. An exceptions file that accumulates bare column
names becomes a place to silence the check, and then the check is worthless —
which is how scripts/schema-index.json ended up stale for eleven days.
Before adding an entry, ask which of these it is:
1. Local bookkeeping the till never sends  -> localOnlyColumns
2. Server-derived, so the till must NOT send it -> ignoreColumns[table]
3. Neither -> it is real drift. Fix the schema, not this file.

_localOnlyColumnReasons.sync_status: Per-row push state on the till: pending | synced | conflict. Verified absent from every push payload — pushLocalRecords selects an explicit column list that excludes it, and it is meaningless server-side because the server is the destination.
_localOnlyColumnReasons.synced_at: When the till last pulled this row. Local cache metadata; the server has no concept of a particular terminal's freshness.
_localOnlyColumnReasons.seq: Phase 1 per-device replication sequence (localDb v45): the LAN outbox/cursor checkpoint between a till and its branch node. Verified absent from every cloud push payload — pushLocalRecords and the sync arms name explicit column lists that exclude it (it appears only in WHERE scoping). Cloud replication keys on ids and idempotency, never on this counter; sending it would mean the server storing one terminal's private LAN checkpoint as data.

_ignoreColumnReasons.payments.business_id: Forced from the caller's token server-side (routes/sync.ts: 'forced from token, not the client'). The till MUST NOT send it — accepting a client-supplied business_id would let one tenant write rows into another.
_ignoreColumnReasons.payments.branch_id: Resolved server-side from the parent order. Sending it from the till would allow a payment to be attributed to a branch the order does not belong to.
_ignoreColumnReasons.customer_credit_transactions.balance_aft: A running balance, computed server-side. A client-supplied value would let an offline till rewrite a customer's credit history.
_ignoreColumnReasons.expenses.device_id: Local-only for now: added by the Phase 1 ownership work (local v44) so own-row scoping and node replication can attribute the row; the cloud push SELECT deliberately omits it and Postgres has no column. Postgres-side attribution for expenses is planned as migration 53 in the Phase 2a batch — when that lands, REMOVE this entry, add the column to the push SELECT, and let parity enforce the pair.
_ignoreColumnReasons.float_transactions.device_id: Same as expenses.device_id — Phase 1 local attribution, omitted from the push, Postgres column pending migration 53. Remove this entry when 53 lands.

_localOnlyTableReasons.session: Owner/device auth state for this terminal.
_localOnlyTableReasons.staff_session: The cashier currently signed in at this terminal.
_localOnlyTableReasons.device_config: Terminal identity and role — device_id, terminal_code, node secret.
_localOnlyTableReasons.sync_queue: The till's own outbound queue. A Postgres table of the same name exists and is unrelated.
_localOnlyTableReasons.local_price_edits: Branch price edits awaiting push; reconciled through /api/branch-prices/sync, not the generic sync path.

_postgresOnlyTablesNote: Left empty deliberately: the till holding a subset of Postgres is the normal case and needs no declaration. Only the reverse is dangerous.
